notes: The two `אֵין` + `לְ` + suffix clauses are read under rule 43: the negation on `אַיִן`, the *had* on the possessive `לְ`, the subject pronoun on the suffix; the clause is verbless, so the preposition is what makes it possessive.
`מִיַּד` is split rather than fused because the ASV spends *on* on the preposition and *the side* on the construct noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet (subtraction test).
`הָעֲשֻׁקִים` takes the substantival *such as* on its article (rule 41), so the construct `דִּמְעַת` takes a supplied *the* of its own (rules 29, 41).

*there was power* is read as rule 20's presentative frame on the predicate noun; the competing reading treats `מִיַּד עֹשְׁקֵיהֶם` as the predicate and would put the copula on the preposition under rule 49, but that preposition already holds *on*.
